question: Replace the search-snippet [S] DAFgiving360 values in donor-behaviour-metrics-2021-2026.csv with first-party text: read the FY2025 Giving Report, the CY2025 release (2026-01-27) and the FY2026 release (2026-07-28) from dafgiving360.org once its robots.txt can be read (it returned 403 on 2026-11-15), and record median grant, recurring share, GivingTuesday 2024/2025 counts and dollars, disaster totals by event, and any account or donor-age figures
conclusion_affected: DAFgiving360 rows (median $500, 38-40% recurring, GT2025 $80m '+37%' vs ~+16% computed, disaster $148m FY2025 / $200m CY2025)

question: Find a public month-of-year series for DAF grants (share in December, GivingTuesday week) for 2021-2026 from a recipient-side or rail source - e.g. Candid's public DAF dashboard, Chariot/DAFpay published seasonality, or GivingTuesday Data Commons DAF tables - and compare it with Vanguard Charitable's ~22% of CY2024 grant count in December and Daffy's ~43% of 2025 contributions in December
conclusion_affected: Timing section: whether December concentration of DAF grants is ~20-25% (Vanguard) or higher; GivingTuesday share
rationale: Only Vanguard publishes a December share (by grant count, one year) and only Daffy a December contribution total; Fidelity publishes only a single GivingTuesday day (48,000 grants, >$129m). No sponsor publishes monthly grant dollars, so cross-sponsor seasonality is unmeasured.

question: Is there any public age, generation or gender breakdown of DAF account holders (not general-population donors) for 2021-2026? Check the methodology and crosstab appendices of the BofA 2026 Study of Wealthy Americans and 2025 Study of Philanthropy (HTML pages only; BofA robots.txt disallows *.pdf), Fidelity Charitable's 2026 'guidance gap' study and 2021 Women and Giving study, and DAFRC publications
conclusion_affected: Demographics section: the only DAF-holder age statistic is BofA 2026 (9% of wealthy use a DAF; 20% of Gen Z/Millennial wealthy)
rationale: No sponsor giving report (Fidelity, Vanguard, DAFgiving360, Daffy, Charityvest) publishes donor age or gender; the generational figures found are general-population surveys (Vanguard/Harris 2023) or wealthy-household surveys (BofA). The next-gen claim behind AI-native entry theses therefore rests on one survey.
